title: Program Management Office and Implementation Lifecycle for Large-Scale Vehicle Inspection Programs
capability_statement: Parsons stands up a dedicated Program Management Office (PMO) immediately upon contract award to plan, transition, implement, and operate large vehicle emissions and safety inspection programs end-to-end. The approach covers a Management Plan and Project Management Plan (PMP), kickoff meeting, weekly transition meetings, weekly and monthly status reports, technical meetings, invoicing, and end-of-contract transition activities; transition of stations, kiosks, hardware, software, and materials; staffing, training, audit, and compliance functions; deliverable development with technical and quality reviews and Acceptance Test Procedures (ATP); and change-management with State approval. Parsons backs this with a deep, in-place corporate structure (two business units: Critical Infrastructure and Federal Solutions), agile and innovative delivery methods (e.g., Zephyr-tracked Agile development for system testing), and an in-place team that mitigates transition and labor-market risk on day one. named_past_performance.name: Pennsylvania Vehicle Emissions I/M Program (PennDOT)
named_past_performance.scope: Full Emissions Program Management for one of the largest, longest-running decentralized I/M programs in the U.S., covering ~8,200 stations across 25 counties and an estimated ~7 million inspections by 2025; services include VIID development and operation, station and inspector compliance/audit (overt and covert), I&E communications, training, court testimony in support of sanctions, and support for legacy connectivity and multiple equipment platforms.
named_past_performance.outcome: Continuous program operation since 1997; in 2012 seamlessly transitioned more than 8,000 stations to Parsons' VIID with no service disruption; in 2016 supported revision of the OBD inspection equipment specification and performed acceptance testing to certify equipment; over 80 million transactions processed to date; 99.99% VIID uptime cited; no security or performance issues on the Pennsylvania VIID.

differentiators: In-place team and corporate resources mean transition risk is minimized on day one rather than being absorbed by the client; Parsons is the only contractor in the cited program that can guarantee no financial or business relationship with currently certified emissions equipment manufacturers, eliminating conflicts of interest. A Program Manager (Jim Valerio) with 12 years' direct prior tenure as full-time general manager of the inspection program brings deep institutional knowledge, supported by named bench (Jason Freeman, 30-year I/M veteran with 25 years' direct State program experience; Navin Dass as Testing Station Transition and Overall Implementation Manager; Robert Suess as Corporate Executive Sponsor; Mike Butler, Bonnie McPherson, John Ott, Darryl McCarthy on the PennDOT-side leadership). Parsons applies Agile development with Zephyr test-case tracking so system testing begins earlier and produces electronic, easily accessible test documentation for State oversight. The OWN ZERO safety culture, NSC-recognized safety standards, and a dedicated Vehicle Inspection and Compliance division of 500+ industry professionals provide depth most competitors cannot match. Recent corporate-dossier acquisitions (e.g., Xator, IPKeys, SealingTech, BlackSignal, BCC Engineering, Chesapeake Technology International, Altamira) and a CEO with seven Wash100 wins, NACD cyber governance certification, and a track record across Federal Solutions and Critical Infrastructure business units underline the financial and technical depth available to back implementation commitments.
